about: Raw archive names and what the name rule makes of each. 'normalized' is the name sent (empty means no name); null means refused. 'repeat' repeats both 'raw' and 'normalized' that many times. Run by arcommon's names tests and by the browser's archiveName tests.

cases.why: an ordinary name is kept as typed
spaces around and between words collapse to one
spaces only is no name at all
empty is no name at all
a tab is refused, never turned into a space
a line feed would start a new receipt line
a carriage return would too
C1 next-line is refused
DEL is refused
a line separator is refused
a paragraph separator is refused
a right-to-left override is refused
a first-strong isolate is refused
the Arabic letter mark is refused
a left-to-right mark is refused
a no-break space is a character, not a space, so it survives trimming
an ideographic space is a character too
a zero-width joiner is allowed; it builds emoji
accented and CJK text is kept
a quote and a colon are ordinary characters
a hundred astral characters is exactly the cap
a hundred and one is over it
the cap is on the normalised length, so padding does not count
